discovered-from:LP-0MWLZ68SF0052E7Z

## Finding

A `implement.py finish` in one item's worktree was failed by the **pre-lock dev-push full-suite
gate** with `reason: full_suite_red`, `failure_kind: infrastructure`, even though the suite passed:

```
Dev-push full-suite verdict is RED for tree d245c11691cee7761d3d5f18f685290b93863843
(reason: infrastructure). Resolved before the finish lock was taken, so nothing was
committed or pushed and local dev was not advanced.
No structured test failures were parsed.
Live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for
.../wl-LP-0MWLZ68SF0052E7Z-... in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/llm:
  added path [??] .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_prefill_eta_pricing_basis.py
  added path [??] proxy/tests/test_local_admission_stamp_consistency.py
  added path [??] proxy/tests/test_measured_basis_eta_pricing.py
```

Facts:

- Suite result: **1208 passed, 2 skipped in 35.7 s** (plus the hidden skill suite); no test failures.
- The three untracked paths are **not** in the finishing item's change set (docs + one new script +
  its test). They are test files another, concurrent herdr-driven implement session was authoring in
  the **main checkout**; they had vanished by the time the gate reported. Main-checkout `HEAD` was
  also advanced by that session (`33193b28c` → `bedbb57c6`) during the run.
- Consequence: item released to `open`, ~10 min of suite work discarded, and a retry was needed.
  The retry (after fast-forwarding the worktree onto the newer `dev`) succeeded and — correctly, by
  design — served the green from the **change-set** cache for the identical patch.

This is the third recorded occurrence: LP-0MVVXGLTM008ROJ9 (`LP-0MWL4O2Z1007KAG4`) and
LP-0MVZF4SU10032OZH (`LP-0MWJUVZKY001Z442`) recorded the same shape, both as **record-only** chores
(i.e. the block was documented and resolved by waiting, never fixed). Earlier guard work
(SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM, SA-0MVXVESV5002HWTW, SA-0MVXPPN22001FS5L, SA-0MV0EFEAB006X79B,
SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8) addressed cross-checkout attribution, `wl sync` churn and ownership exclusion;
foreign **untracked file creation in the main checkout during the suite** still fails an unrelated
item's finish.

## Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want a concurrent session's transient churn in the main
checkout to be excluded from (or re-baselined out of) my gate verdict, so a green suite is not
discarded because somebody else was authoring files — while the guard keeps failing on *my* own
mutation and on any mutation the suite itself causes in a guarded checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Foreign churn cannot fail the verdict.** A run whose diff-versus-baseline consists only of
  paths outside the finishing item's change set (not in its would-be-commit tree, not owned by its
  worktree) reports the suite's real verdict; those paths are recorded as
  `foreign_churn_excluded` evidence instead of `full_suite_red`/`infrastructure`.
- **AC2 — Guard still fails closed on real mutations.** The verdict is still red when (a) a path in
  the item's own change set is mutated after the baseline, or (b) the suite mutates a guarded
  checkout, or (c) the baseline cannot be established — each with a named reason.
- **AC3 — Regression tests.** A test drives a finish/suite run while a *foreign* writer creates and
  removes an untracked file in the main checkout and asserts the run completes with the suite's
  verdict; a paired test asserts the item's own late mutation still fails. No real sleeps: use the
  existing hook/fixture seams.
- **AC4 — Actionable message.** When the gate does fail on churn, the message names the owning
  item/worktree/session when determinable, so the operator can see whose work caused it (today it
  names only the finishing item).
- **AC5 — Suite + docs.** Full suite green through the test skill; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (or the
  guard's own doc) states the foreign-churn rule.

## Notes

- Not to be confused with the *change-set cache* behaviour seen on the retry (a rebased,
  patch-identical push serving a green verdict): that is intended (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC), but it does
  mean the **pushed tree** was never itself full-suite-tested — worth stating in the doc alongside
  AC5.
- Root cause candidates to check first: the baseline is captured on the *main checkout* while the
  change set lives in a *linked worktree*, so "paths absent from the baseline" and "paths not in the
  item's tree" are conflated; ownership exclusion may only apply to paths the runner knows about
  (`git_sandbox`), not to untracked creations in the shared checkout.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (pre-lock full-suite verdict, `main_checkout_guard`,
  `_gate_failure_kind`/`_gate_failure_detail`, `resolve_prelock_full_suite_verdict`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (guard baseline / ownership exclusion)
- `skill/implement/tests/` (finish-gate and guard regression tests)

## Impact

An agent finishing a work item keeps the suite's real verdict when another session happens to be writing files at the same time, instead of losing ~10 minutes of suite work and a claim to a false red.
data.title: [bug] Finish gate discards a green suite when a concurrent session creates files in the main checkout (foreign churn)

data.description:
# Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose

## Problem statement

SorraAgents skills recover a work item's acceptance criteria by regexing the
`## Acceptance Criteria` section out of the work item's `description` (canonical
implementation: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria`).
Worklog is adding a first-class `acceptance_criteria` table with one row per
criterion — stable id, ordering, text, status (`met|unmet|partial|modified`)
and, for `modified` rows, the original text plus the justification. Skills must
switch from prose parsing to the table so a criterion has identity and status.

## Users

- **Pi agent sessions** that run skills consuming acceptance criteria programmatically: `audit`, `implement`, `find-related`, `plan`, `intake`, `report`.
- **Developer** maintaining those skills — needs predictable, testable AC behaviour regardless of description edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every skill that extracts acceptance criteria programmatically reads them from
  the worklog table (`wl ac show <id> --json`) instead of parsing description
  text; `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` either
  delegates to the table or remains only as an explicit legacy/description
  fallback, with the fallback documented and tested.
- `find-related` and `implement` are updated first (as named in the parent
  request) to use the AC rows rather than a full `wl show` where the table
  suffices.
- AC-coverage review (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::compute_coverage` /
  `apply_coverage_review`) compares criteria rows — by id where both sides are
  migrated, by similarity only for unmigrated descriptions — and its behaviour
  is covered by tests.
- Per-criterion status is honoured where the skills already reason about
  criteria (audit reports, plan coverage, intake briefs): a `met` criterion does
  not count as a gap, and a `modified` criterion is shown with its original text
  and justification.
- Skills remain functional against a store that has **not** yet run `wl doctor
  upgrade` (no AC rows): the fallback path is exercised by a test.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop re-parsing acceptance criteria out of prose and read them as
addressable rows with their own status, so a criterion can be cited by id and a
re-worded criterion is visibly `modified` rather than silently different.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the Worklog store beyond the existing `wl` CLI surface: no
  writes to the `acceptance_criteria` table from the skills.
- The skills ship from this repository; the table is delivered by ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG`. Do not implement schema or CLI changes here.
- `AC status is advisory in this phase` (ContextHub decision Q3 = advisory): no
  skill may gate closure on AC status yet — 15,172 back-filled criteria start as
  `unmet`.
- **Blocking dependency**: this work cannot be implemented until the ContextHub
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (Add a table for ACs) delivers the `wl ac` CLI and
  back-fill. That item is `blocked`/`plan_complete`. This item must be marked
  blocked-on that dependency.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` parses prose from
  `## Acceptance Criteria` headings using regex/line-scanning.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py::run_wl_show` fetches a full
  `wl show` to read descriptions (and indirectly, AC prose).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` extracts AC lines internally and
  supports `adjusted` verdicts in its own vocabulary but does not yet use the
  AC table.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` accepts `acceptance_criteria` rows
  but only from the render_report CLI, not from skills.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`
  reference AC coverage via prose-parsed lists.

## Desired change

All skills that programmatically consume ACs delegate to `wl ac show <id> --json`
(or an equivalent table-read helper). Where the AC table is absent (pre-migration
stores), a documented fallback reads prose. AC-coverage comparison uses row ids
when available, falls back to string similarity when not.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Migration window risk:** Both prose-fallback and table-backed code paths must
  coexist during the transition. Any regression in prose-fallback will break
  skills against un-migrated stores.
  *Mitigation:* exhaustive fallback tests before table migration; phased rollout.
- **Scope creep:** All listed skills (tree_coverage, find-related, implement, plan,
  intake, audit, report) in a single change-set is large. Risk of merge conflicts
  and review fatigue.
  *Mitigation:* implement in dependency order (tree_coverage → find-related →
  implement → audit → report → skill docs).
- **Assumption:** the `wl ac show` CLI surface (JSON shape) stabilises before
  implementation begins. If it changes, the table-adapter in tree_coverage will
  need revision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — needs table-backed AC reads and the
  documented legacy fallback.
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — needs AC rows instead of a
  full `wl show` where possible.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — needs the AC workflow to read rows.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — need the coverage/brief
  paths updated.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — needs its per-criterion verdicts
  reconciled with the table's status vocabulary (`adjusted` ≈ `modified`).
- `skill/shared/tests/` — needs coverage tests for table-backed reads plus the
  no-AC-rows fallback.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the `wl ac` CLI already available in the SorraAgents environment?"
  — Answer (research): No. `wl ac --help` is not found; the ContextHub item
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` is `blocked` / `plan_complete`. This is a hard block
  — implementation cannot start until ContextHub delivers.
- Q: "Which skills are in-scope for the initial table-backed migration?"
  — Answer (from description): `tree_coverage` (core), `find-related`,
  `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `audit`, `report`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWB84J17008N4QF** – audit_runner _extract_acs treats prose mentioning 'acceptance criteria' as the AC heading — parent ACs silently unevaluated (completed)
- **SA-0MW6ZZ1HR009DD9Q** – Close coverage gap: **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no... (completed)
- **SA-0MP3YN1HH000SCX9** – make success criteria and acceptance criteria synonyms (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, adding, adjusted (+159 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, advisory, agents (+156 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, adjusted, agents (+150 more)

# Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want regression tests that prove a concurrent session's transient churn in the main checkout cannot abort my finish or fail my suite, while a mutation I caused — or one the suite caused in a guarded checkout — still fails, so the fix cannot silently regress into the reported incident.

# Context

- Today `implement.py::_main_checkout_guard_violations` treats *any* path that becomes dirty in the main checkout between the Step-0.75 baseline and a verify point as offending, including a foreign session's `??` untracked creation. `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_violations_report_new_untracked_path` (line 85) pins that as intended, so the reported incident still reproduces one step later than the pre-lock suite gate: the `pre_push` verify aborts, the item is released to `open`, and an already-green suite is discarded.
- The suite guard's half is already fixed and pinned (`skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py::test_guarded_run_ignores_main_checkout_churn[untracked-creation]`); this item must pin the finish half plus the paired negative cases.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC3 — Regression tests: a test drives a finish/suite run while a *foreign* writer creates and removes an untracked file in the main checkout and asserts the run completes with the suite's verdict; a paired test asserts the item's own late mutation still fails. No real sleeps: use the existing hook/fixture seams.
- AC3 (finish half, present-at-verify variant): a second scripted case leaves the foreign untracked file present at the final verify and asserts the run still completes with the suite's verdict and records the path as excluded evidence.
- AC2 — Guard still fails closed on real mutations, case (a): the paired test asserts the verdict is still red when a path in the item's own change set is mutated after the baseline; case (b): a guarded checkout mutated by the suite is still red.
- The guarded-root (worktree) negative case is asserted too, so narrowing the main-checkout role can never widen into the guarded root.
- The new tests fail against the current tree and pass after the implementation siblings land; the changed-scope gate via the test skill is green.

# Minimal Implementation

- Add finish-guard cases to `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, reusing `_finish_harness`, `_snapshots`, `_tests_result`, `patch.object(implement, "_snapshot_main_checkout", side_effect=...)`.
- Add the guarded-root negative case to `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` beside the existing `_MAIN_CHECKOUT_CHURN_CASES` parametrisation.
- Add the pure-predicate unit cases beside the existing classification tests in `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` (mirroring `test_violations_report_new_untracked_path` after it is repurposed).

# Risky assumptions

- The existing `_finish_harness` supports scripting three snapshots (baseline, `pre_push`, `pre_worktree_removal`) — it does today for `test_finish_abort_before_worktree_removal_leaves_item_open`. Verify before adding cases.

# Dependencies

None. Blocks F2, F3 and F4 of the parent.

# Deliverables

- Finish-guard regression tests (foreign churn excluded; own late mutation and foreign deletion still abort).
- Guarded-root negative test in the suite-guard suite.
- Predicate-level unit cases for the new status-class rule.

## Key Files

- skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py
- skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/shared/git_sandbox.py

## Impact

An agent finishing a work item keeps the suite's verdict when a concurrent session writes to the main checkout, because that shape is pinned by a test instead of being re-learned from an incident.

parent: SA-0MWRXHIAC007CNAP
test-first: blocked by the parent's test item — this implementation lands after its regression tests exist.

# Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want `finish`'s main-checkout guard to exclude a concurrent session's path churn in the main checkout (untracked creations, modifications, staged additions) from its verdict — recording it as `foreign_churn_excluded` evidence naming the likely owner — while it keeps failing closed on a tracked-file deletion and on any mutation of the guarded checkout, so a green suite is not discarded because somebody else was authoring files.

# Context

- `implement.py::_main_checkout_guard_violations` currently returns every path whose status entry changed between `_snapshot_main_checkout` baselines unless it is under `.worklog/`, a project expected-dirty path, or non-deletion `own_churn`. It has no role or status-class scoping, so a foreign `??` creation aborts the run at the `pre_push` / `pre_worktree_removal` verify.
- The suite guard already applies exactly the rule needed: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_role_scope_main_checkout_diff` + `_reports_tracked_deletion` narrow the MAIN_CHECKOUT role to the tracked-file-deletion class. **Reuse it rather than re-implementing it** — the operator doc already asserts the attribution rule lives in the shared helper so consumers cannot drift.
- `implement.py` already owns the attribution plumbing this feature needs: `_main_checkout_actor_evidence`, `_annotate_excluded_churn_notes`, `_main_checkout_guard_message`, and the `report["live_repo_excluded"]` / `report["live_repo_actor_evidence"]` fields that `_gate_failure_detail` renders.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Foreign churn cannot fail the verdict: a finish run whose diff-versus-baseline consists only of paths outside the finishing item's change set (not in its would-be-commit tree, not owned by its worktree) reports the suite's real verdict, and those paths are recorded as `foreign_churn_excluded` evidence (aliased as `live_repo_excluded`) instead of `full_suite_red`/`infrastructure`.
- AC2 — Guard still fails closed on real mutations, case (b): the verdict is still red when the suite mutates a guarded checkout, and a tracked-file deletion in the main checkout stays offending (`D` in either column), preserving the 2026-10-26 `packages/shared` wipe class; `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_violations_report_new_untracked_path` is repurposed into an exclusion assertion rather than deleted.
- The rule is applied only to the resolved main-checkout root: a path in the guarded checkout (the worktree) that becomes dirty after the baseline remains offending, pinned by a unit case that passes a non-main role root.
- The narrowing predicate is shared, not forked: the status-class rule comes from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, and a unit test asserts the finish guard and `diff_guarded_roots` agree on the deletion class for the same status codes (`D `, ` D`, `DD`, ` M`, `M `, `MM`, `??`).
- Excluded evidence never disappears silently: `_verify_main_checkout` records it on the verify entry and `phase_finish` surfaces it in the JSON report and the log, keeping the existing `Live-repo guard note:` log line.
- The changed-scope gate via the test skill is green.

# Minimal Implementation

- Export the status-class predicate from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (make `_reports_tracked_deletion` public or add a thin `is_main_checkout_narrowed_status(code)` wrapper) — no behaviour change to `_role_scope_main_checkout_diff`.
- In `_main_checkout_guard_violations`, split between offending paths and narrowed/excluded paths: keep `.worklog/`, expected-dirty, `own_churn` and deletion handling as-is, add the shared status-class exclusion for the main-checkout root, and return the excluded list alongside the violations.
- Thread the excluded list through `_verify_main_checkout` (new `excluded` field on the verify entry and a `guard["foreign_churn_excluded"]` accumulator) and into `phase_finish`'s report + log, reusing `_annotate_excluded_churn_notes` for the actor signal.
- Keep the guard's contract in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` consistent (the follow-up docs item covers the prose; this item must not leave `test_guard_docs.py` red).

# Risky assumptions

- `_main_checkout_guard_violations` gains a return shape change; every caller and the existing classification tests must be updated in the same commit. Grep for all call sites (`_verify_main_checkout` is the only production caller).

# Dependencies

Blocked by the parent's test item (F1).

# Deliverables

- Shared status-class predicate exported from `git_sandbox`.
- Finish guard narrowing with `foreign_churn_excluded` / `live_repo_excluded` evidence and actor annotation.
- Report/log surfacing of the excluded churn.

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/shared/git_sandbox.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Impact

An agent finishing a work item no longer loses a green suite — and an hour of work — because another session happened to be writing files in the main checkout at the same time.

parent: SA-0MWRXHIAC007CNAP
test-first: blocked by the parent's test item — this implementation lands after its regression tests exist.

# Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want an unestablishable guard baseline to fail closed with a named reason, instead of silently reporting a clean guard, so the foreign-churn exemption of the sibling feature can never turn into a blind spot.

# Context

- `implement.py::git_status` swallows a non-zero `git status` (returns `""`), so `_main_checkout_status_map` yields `{}` and `_snapshot_main_checkout` produces an empty baseline. `_main_checkout_guard_violations` then compares `{}` against the verify snapshot and reports every path as offending — or, worse, with an empty current snapshot, reports `pass` while the guard was never able to look.
- On the suite side, `_detect_live_repo_mutation` returns `{"mutation": None, ...}` when `snapshot_before is None`, and `snapshot_guarded_roots` degrades to empty surfaces for a non-git root, so the guard can be a silent no-op.
- AC2(c): "the baseline cannot be established — each with a named reason".

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC2 — Guard still fails closed on real mutations, case (c): the verdict is still red when the baseline cannot be established, each with a named reason (`guard_baseline_unavailable`) recorded on the guard report and named in the operator-facing message, instead of `verdict: "pass"`.
- When the Step-0.75 baseline snapshot cannot be established (`git status` fails, the root is not a working tree, or the snapshot is empty for a non-empty checkout), `phase_finish` refuses and the item is released to `open`; the report records the reason and the absent surface.
- The refusal is distinguishable from a foreign-churn exclusion and from a real mutation: the reason vocabulary is enumerated in the guard report.
- When `_snapshot_main_checkout` cannot be established at a *verify* point, the run likewise refuses with the named reason instead of treating the unreadable surface as clean.
- On the suite side, a guarded run whose `snapshot_before` is `None` while a guard was expected (the guard-ownership marker was set) reports a named infrastructure reason instead of returning no verdict; a genuinely non-git root stays the documented no-op.
- Named reasons are stable machine-readable codes, consistent with the existing `_gate_failure_kind` / `gate_reason.classify_gate_result` vocabulary rather than free prose.
- The changed-scope gate via the test skill is green.

# Minimal Implementation

- Give `_snapshot_main_checkout` an explicit availability signal (return `{"available": False, "reason": ...}` or raise a typed error) instead of an empty status map; update `_main_checkout_guard_violations` / `_verify_main_checkout` to short-circuit to the named reason.
- Add the reason code to the guard report contract (`report["steps"]["main_checkout_guard"]["reason"]`) and to `_main_checkout_guard_message`.
- For the suite side, make `guarded_run_all` record a `guard_baseline_unavailable` notice when `guard_active` is true and the baseline snapshot was not captured, reusing the existing `notices` plumbing so `_gate_failure_kind` classifies it as infrastructure.
- Keep `snapshot_repo_state`'s documented non-git no-op behaviour intact.

# Risky assumptions

- Some call sites snapshot the main checkout for advisory/report-only purposes (the refactor verify). Confirm the refusal applies only to verdict-bearing verifies, so an advisory step cannot become a new abort source (the SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG false-positive class).

# Dependencies

Blocked by the parent's test item (F1). Independent of the sibling scoping feature (F2), but both touch `_verify_main_checkout` — sequence after it if conflicts appear.

# Deliverables

- Explicit baseline-availability signal on both guards.
- Named `guard_baseline_unavailable` reason in the finish report, message and suite notices.

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Impact

An agent finishing a work item can tell the difference between "the guard looked and found nothing" and "the guard could not look", so a silent blind spot can never be mistaken for a clean run.

data.description:
parent: SA-0MWRXHIAC007CNAP
test-first: blocked by the parent's test item — this implementation lands after its regression tests exist.

# Goal

As an operator reading a failed gate, I want the failure message to name *whose* work caused the churn — the owning work item, worktree path and session when determinable — instead of only naming the finishing item, so I can act on it instead of investigating from scratch.

# Context

- `implement.py::_main_checkout_actor_evidence` already delegates to the shared read-only `shared.concurrent_actor.describe_concurrent_actor` (names the likely owner from `.implement_state.json` files, one bounded `wl` claim lookup, the lock holder and live `/proc` sessions, falling back to `"unknown"`), and `_main_checkout_guard_message` already renders `Concurrent actor evidence: <evidence>`.
- `run_tests._detect_live_repo_mutation` appends `Concurrent actor evidence:` to the mutation message **only** `if main_mutated`, and only as one opaque string. AC4 requires the owning item/worktree/session to be named when determinable, on the gate failure path itself.
- `shared/concurrent_actor` already exposes the individual signals (`describe_concurrent_actor`, `annotate_excluded_notes`, `actor_evidence_from_note`) — reuse them, do not add a second attribution implementation.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC4 — Actionable message: when the gate does fail on churn, the message names the owning item/worktree/session when determinable, so the operator can see whose work caused it (today it names only the finishing item).
- When the owner is determinable the rendered failure detail names the owning work item id, the owning worktree path and the session identity where available; when nothing is determinable it says `unknown` explicitly rather than omitting the line.
- The attribution is attached to the *failure* path (`live_repo_mutation` and the finish guard's abort message) and not only to the excluded-churn note, so a red verdict names the culprit.
- The attribution is additive: it never changes the verdict, and a failing or missing attribution helper degrades to `unknown` without raising (the existing fail-open contract).
- The bounded lookup still runs at most once per guarded run in the suite path, and is never performed on a clean run or in the per-test guard path.
- Structured evidence is available to `--json` consumers (a field on the mutation/guard report entry, not only in prose), so tooling can key on the owner.
- The changed-scope gate via the test skill is green.

# Minimal Implementation

- Extend the shared `concurrent_actor` renderer to return the individual signals (item, worktree path, session) in addition to its prose summary, keeping the existing prose API backward compatible.
- Attach the structured evidence to `live_repo_mutation` (e.g. a `mutation_actor` field on the run result) and to the finish guard's verify entry, and render it in `_gate_failure_detail` and `_main_checkout_guard_message`.
- Remove the `if main_mutated` narrowness so a mutation of the guarded root also names the discoverable actor when there is one, without changing which checkouts are verdict-bearing.

# Risky assumptions

Planning Complete — decomposition, research findings and Appendix. (plan skill, SA-0MWRXHIAC007CNAP)

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-11-26: initial plan — 5 features (test-first), findings recorded, AC coverage review applied (`proceed`, 100% parent-AC coverage).
- 2026-11-26: normalised the parent description's section headings from `#` to `##` (no wording change). The AC section previously never terminated — the extractor treats only `##` as a section boundary — so `## Notes` and `## Key Files` bullets were parsed as acceptance criteria (10 ACs instead of the real 5). Fixing the heading level is what lets the AC coverage review see the real criteria set.

## Seed Context
- **Title:** [bug] Finish gate discards a green suite when a concurrent session creates files in the main checkout (foreign churn)
- **Type:** bug · **Priority:** medium · **Effort:** M · **Risk:** Medium · **Stage on entry:** intake_complete
- **Discovered from:** LP-0MWLZ68SF0052E7Z (third recorded occurrence of this shape).

## Repo research — what is already fixed, and what is still open

### Already implemented on `dev` (do not re-implement)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_role_scope_main_checkout_diff` (WL-0MWR1OXHX001KJC6, commit `8261c30e9f`) narrows the **main checkout** role of `diff_guarded_roots` to the tracked-file-deletion class: a newly dirty ` M`, `M `, `MM`, `??` or staged-addition path there moves to `excluded.status.narrowed` and is rendered by `excluded_churn_notes`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_detect_live_repo_mutation` already returns `live_repo_excluded` notes plus actor evidence, `guarded_run_all` carries them on the result, and `implement.py::_gate_failure_detail` already renders an "Excluded foreign churn (not counted in the verdict)" section, while `phase_finish` records `report["live_repo_excluded"]` / `report["live_repo_actor_evidence"]`.
- Regression pin: `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py::test_guarded_run_ignores_main_checkout_churn[untracked-creation]`.
- **Conclusion:** the incident's *pre-lock dev-push full-suite* path is already fixed on `dev`. The reported run was based on an older `dev` than commit `8261c30e9f` (the report itself notes `dev` advanced `33193b28c` → `bedbb57c6` during the run).

### Still open — the remaining defect this item must fix
1. **`implement.py::_main_checkout_guard_violations` has no role/status-class scoping.** Every path that becomes dirty in the main checkout between the Step-0.75 baseline (`_snapshot_main_checkout`) and a verify point is offending — including a foreign session's `??` untracked creation. That behaviour is currently pinned as *intended* by `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_violations_report_new_untracked_path` (line 85). The identical incident therefore still reproduces one step later: the `pre_push` / `pre_worktree_removal` verify (`_verify_main_checkout` → `_abort_on_main_checkout_violation`) aborts with "Main-checkout mutation detected", the item is released to `open`, and an already-green suite is discarded.
2. **No `foreign_churn_excluded` evidence key exists** anywhere in the tree (AC1 names it); the existing key is `live_repo_excluded`.
3. **An unestablishable baseline fails open.** `_main_checkout_status_map` returns `{}` when `git status` exits non-zero (`git_status` swallows the failure and returns `""`), so a guard whose baseline could not be taken silently reports `pass`; `_detect_live_repo_mutation` likewise returns `mutation: None` when `snapshot_before is None`. AC2(c) requires a named red reason instead.
4. **AC4 attribution gap.** The pre-lock suite mutation message appends `Concurrent actor evidence:` only `if main_mutated`, and the finish guard message carries one evidence string — it does not name the owning worktree/session path when determinable.
5. **Docs.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` does not exist. The guard's own docs are `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (§ Finish main-checkout guard) and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` (§8.5 shared rule + excluded-bucket JSON contract). AC5's "or the guard's own doc" clause covers this. The change-set ("patch") cache caveat in the item's Notes is not stated there.

### Reuse decision
Do **not** fork the narrowing rule. Extract/reuse the shared `git_sandbox` predicate (`_reports_tracked_deletion` plus the same status-class rule `_role_scope_main_checkout_diff` applies) so the finish guard and the suite guard cannot drift — which is exactly what `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` already claims ("the attribution rule itself lives in the shared `git_sandbox` helper, so the inner `live_repo_guard` plugin cannot drift from it").

## Proposed features (test-first)

| # | Type | Title | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | task (test) | Regression tests: foreign churn cannot abort a finish | — |
| F2 | task (impl) | Scope the finish main-checkout guard to foreign churn | F1 |
| F3 | task (impl) | Fail closed with a named reason when the guard baseline is unavailable | F1 |
| F4 | task (impl) | Name the owning item/worktree/session in churn messages | F1, F2 |
| F5 | docs | Document the foreign-churn rule and patch-cache caveat | F2, F3, F4 |

Created: F1 `SA-0MWY70JFR000BVLY`, F2 `SA-0MWY70O6E001WZXS`, F3 `SA-0MWY70QEB008JTHZ`, F4 `SA-0MWY70SY1000Y0NI`, F5 `SA-0MWY70UQM009DFYA`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Where must the foreign-churn exclusion apply — the pre-lock dev-push suite guard, finish's own main-checkout guard, or both?**
  Answer (agent, repo research): Both, but only finish's guard is still unscoped. Evidence: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_role_scope_main_checkout_diff` (commit `8261c30e9f`, WL-0MWR1OXHX001KJC6) already narrows the suite guard, pinned by `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py::test_guarded_run_ignores_main_checkout_churn[untracked-creation]`; `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_main_checkout_guard_violations` does not, pinned by `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_violations_report_new_untracked_path`. Final: both surfaces, F2 targets the finish guard.

- **Q: Should a *foreign tracked-file deletion* in the main checkout also be excluded (AC1 read literally), or stay verdict-bearing?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption): It stays verdict-bearing. Evidence: `_reports_tracked_deletion` deliberately retains the `D` class on the MAIN_CHECKOUT role (WL-0MWR1OXHX001KJC6) so the 2026-10-26 `packages/shared` wipe stays detectable, and AC2(b) ("the suite mutates a guarded checkout" stays red) cannot hold for a deletion if AC1 is applied literally — diff evidence alone cannot distinguish "foreign session deleted it" from "the suite deleted it". **OPEN QUESTION** (directed to the producer; non-blocking): if a foreign session's deletion must also be excluded, attribution evidence rather than the diff would have to become verdict-bearing, which weakens wipe protection. Recorded, run continued on the existing documented contract.

- **Q: Evidence key name — `foreign_churn_excluded` (AC1) or the existing `live_repo_excluded`?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption): Emit both, identical content. `live_repo_excluded` stays canonical (existing contract WL-0MWR1P1F3008AH3V, named in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, consumed by `_gate_failure_detail` and `phase_finish`); `foreign_churn_excluded` is added as the AC1-named alias so the AC is honoured without breaking existing consumers.

- **Q: Which document must state the rule (AC5 names `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`)?**
  Answer (agent, repo research): That file does not exist; AC5's "or the guard's own doc" applies. Targets: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` § Finish main-checkout guard (new foreign-churn rule + report fields) and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 (shared rule / excluded-bucket contract), plus the patch-cache caveat from the item's Notes.

- **Q: How are the AC3 regression tests driven without real sleeps?**
  Answer (agent, repo research): Existing seams only. Finish guard: `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`'s `_finish_harness` + `_snapshots([...])` patches `_snapshot_main_checkout` with a scripted sequence, so a "foreign writer creates then removes an untracked file" is expressed as scripted snapshots. Suite guard: `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py::_sibling_main_checkout_command` makes the *suite command itself* perform the foreign write. Neither needs a sleep.

- **Q: Vertical-slice phasing — does tracer-bullet ordering apply?**
  Answer (agent, documented decision): No. The fix is a predicate change in one shared helper plus its two call sites, so there is no layer-per-phase cut to make; the item is too small to phase. Ordering is therefore test-first (F1) → implementation (F2, F3, F4) → docs (F5), with the description of each successor reviewed after its predecessor lands.

- **Q: Duplicate work?**
  Answer (agent, repo search): `wl search "foreign churn"`, `"live_repo guard checkout mutation"`, `"main checkout churn exclusion"`, `"full_suite_red infrastructure"` reviewed. Five completed siblings listed in the item (SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM, SA-0MVXVESV5002HWTW, SA-0MVXPPN22001FS5L, SA-0MV0EFEAB006X79B, SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8) plus WL-0MWR1OXHX001KJC6 / WL-0MWR1P1F3008AH3V cover attribution, ownership exclusion and the suite guard's narrowing — none closes the finish guard's `??`-creation abort or the baseline-unavailable fail-open. No full duplicate found; no overlapping item was rewritten.
